SAFE AT HOME ADDRESS CONFIDENTIALITY PROGRAM — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc. · Victim of domestic violence

WHAT THIS DOCUMENT COVERS AND HOW IT DIFFERS FROM A RESTRAINING ORDER
This information sheet describes California's Address Confidentiality Program, known as "Safe at Home," which the Secretary of State administers under Government Code sections 6205 through 6210.7 (Chapter 3.1, covering victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, and elder or dependent adult abuse) and sections 6215 through 6216.6 (Chapter 3.2, covering reproductive and gender-affirming health care providers, employees, volunteers, and patients, and other individuals who face threats or violence because of work for a public entity, such as election workers). Safe at Home is an administrative program run by the Secretary of State's office, not a court proceeding: a program participant applies to have mail routed through a substitute address that state and local agencies may accept in place of Acme, Inc.'s actual residential address on public records. It is a separate mechanism from this project's Domestic Violence Restraining Order (DVRO) document: a DVRO is a court order directing a named respondent's conduct toward a petitioner and requires a judge's finding of abuse under Family Code section 6200 et seq., while Safe at Home issues no order against anyone, names no respondent, and does not depend on obtaining or having obtained a restraining order. The two can be used together or separately, and Safe at Home's eligibility categories are broader than domestic violence alone. This document is informational; it does not itself enroll Acme, Inc. in the program, and only the Secretary of State can approve an application.

ELIGIBILITY UNDER THE CORE SAFE AT HOME CHAPTER (CHAPTER 3.1)
Government Code section 6205(a) states the Legislature's finding that persons escaping actual or threatened domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder or dependent adult abuse frequently change names or addresses to avoid their assailants, and that Chapter 3.1 exists to let state and local agencies respond to public records requests without disclosing a program participant's changed name or location. Section 6206(a)(1)(A) requires the applicant's sworn statement that Acme, Inc., or the minor or incapacitated person on whose behalf the application is made, is a victim of one of those same six categories -- domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder or dependent adult abuse -- or is a household member of such a victim, unless the applicant is the perpetrator. Victim of domestic violence states which of these categories the application would be based on.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The Legislature finds that persons attempting to escape from actual or threatened domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder or dependent adult abuse frequently establish new names or addresses to prevent their assailants or probable assailants from finding them."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6205(a), legislative findings and purpose of Chapter 3.1 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6205.)
  "is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder or dependent adult abuse, or is a household member of a victim who is making or has made an application pursuant to this section, unless the applicant is the perpetrator of the crime that provided the basis for that victim’s application."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6206(a)(1)(A), the six qualifying victim categories for the sworn application statement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6206.)
  Known gap: Section 6205(a) and section 6206(a)(1)(A) are two different subdivisions within the same statutory section family but not the same section -- 6205 is a legislative-findings section and 6206 is the separate application-and-certification section -- so this is not a single-section citation, though both are within Chapter 3.1. This is California's own statute, used as evidence of what that state's program covers -- not a claim that every state with an address confidentiality program uses the same six categories, or that any other state recognizes these same terms. Child abduction and elder or dependent adult abuse are included as independent eligibility categories under this chapter alongside the more commonly cited domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, and human trafficking; a household member of a qualifying victim may also independently qualify. This clause does not resolve whether a specific applicant's facts satisfy any category -- that determination is made by the Secretary of State on the application, not by this document.

ELIGIBILITY UNDER THE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CARE AND PUBLIC ENTITY WORKER CHAPTER (CHAPTER 3.2)
A second, separately enacted Safe at Home chapter -- Government Code sections 6215 through 6216.6 -- covers different applicant categories than Chapter 3.1. Section 6215(b) states the Legislature's finding that, since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, individuals who work with the public face increasing harassment, threats, and violence because of that work, giving as examples public health officers and workers, election workers, school board members, and code enforcement officers. Section 6215.1(c) defines a "designated health care services provider, employee, volunteer, or patient" as a gender-affirming health care or gender-affirming mental health care provider, employee, volunteer, or patient, or a reproductive health care services provider, employee, volunteer, or patient. Chapter 3.2 also allows an application on the separate basis that Acme, Inc. is employed by, or performs work under a contract with, a public entity and faces threats, violence, or harassment from the public because of that work.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Other individuals are also subject to harassment, threats, and acts of violence from the public because of their work with the public, which have become more frequent and serious since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. They include, but are not limited to, public health officers and public health workers, election workers, school board members, and code enforcement officers."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6215(b), legislative findings on public entity workers facing threats and violence (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6215.)
  "“Designated health care services provider, employee, volunteer, or patient” means a gender-affirming health care or a gender-affirming mental health care provider, employee, volunteer, or patient, or a reproductive health care services provider, employee, volunteer, or patient."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6215.1(c), definition of a designated health care services provider, employee, volunteer, or patient (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6215.1.)
  Known gap: Section 6215(b) is a legislative-findings subdivision and section 6215.1(c) is a separate definitions section, so this is not a single-section citation. Election workers are named in section 6215(b) only as an illustrative example within the Legislature's findings, not as a standalone defined eligibility category with its own subsection; the operative eligibility basis in section 6215.2(b) is the broader category of a person who works for, or under contract with, a public entity and faces threats or violence because of that work, which sweeps in election workers along with the other named examples and others not named. This chapter also covers gender-affirming health care providers, employees, volunteers, and patients as of a 2025 amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 679), which is broader than "reproductive health care" alone; a research brief describing this program only as covering reproductive health care and election workers would understate both the health-care-services definition and the general public-entity-worker basis. This is California's own statute and does not describe any other state's program.

HOW AN APPLICATION IS FILED AND CERTIFIED
Under Government Code section 6206(a), an applicant to the core Chapter 3.1 program must complete the application in person at a community-based victims' assistance program, or a community-based program serving victims of elder or dependent adult abuse, and the application process must include meeting with a victims' assistance counselor and receiving orientation information about the program. Section 6206(d) provides that once the Secretary of State receives a properly completed application, the Secretary of State certifies the applicant as a program participant, and applicants are certified for four years from the filing date unless certification is withdrawn or invalidated earlier. Acme, Inc. would file the application with the Secretary of State's office, not with a court.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An application shall be completed in person at a community-based victims’ assistance program or a community-based assistance program that serves victims of elder or dependent adult abuse pursuant to the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act (Chapter 11 (commencing with Section 15600) of Part 3 of Division 9 of the Welfare and Institutions Code). The application process shall include a requirement that the applicant meet with a victims’ assistance counselor and receive orientation information about the program."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6206(a), in-person application requirement and counselor orientation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6206.)
  "Upon filing a properly completed application, the Secretary of State shall certify the applicant as a program participant. Applicants shall be certified for four years following the date of filing, unless the certification is withdrawn or invalidated before that date."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6206(d), certification upon a properly completed application and the four-year certification period (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6206.)
  Known gap: Section 6206(a) and section 6206(d) are two subdivisions of the same statutory section, so this is a single-section citation for that pairing. Chapter 3.2 (the reproductive health care and public entity worker chapter) has its own, separately worded application and in-person counseling requirement in section 6215.2(a)-(b) that this clause does not quote; the four-year certification period stated here from section 6206(d) applies to the Chapter 3.1 program, and Chapter 3.2 applies a similar four-year period with a shorter six-month period for designated health care services facility volunteers, per section 6215.2(f). This clause does not describe the specific documentary evidence requirements (police records, sworn statements, and similar supporting materials) in either chapter's application in full detail. This is California's own statute; it does not describe any other state's application procedure.

USE OF THE SUBSTITUTE ADDRESS WITH STATE AND LOCAL AGENCIES
Government Code section 6207(a) provides that when a state or local agency creates a public record, the agency must accept the Secretary of State's designated substitute address as a program participant's address, unless the Secretary of State has determined that the agency has a bona fide statutory or administrative requirement for the actual address and will use that address only for that purpose without public dissemination. Section 6207(b) applies the same substitute-address requirement when an agency modifies or maintains a public record, but expressly excludes birth, fetal death, death, and marriage records registered under the Health and Safety Code. Section 6207(c) additionally allows a program participant to use the designated address as a work address, and section 6207(d) requires the Secretary of State's office to forward first-class mail and government mail to program participants.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "When creating a public record, state and local agencies shall accept the address designated by the Secretary of State as a program participant’s substitute address, unless the Secretary of State has determined both of the following: (1) The agency has a bona fide statutory or administrative requirement for the use of the address which would otherwise be confidential under this chapter. (2) This address will be used only for those statutory and administrative purposes and shall not be publicly disseminated."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6207(a), acceptance of the substitute address when creating a public record (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6207.)
  "When modifying or maintaining a public record, excluding the record of any birth, fetal death, death, or marriage registered under Division 102 (commencing with Section 102100) of the Health and Safety Code, state and local agencies shall accept the address designated by the Secretary of State as a program participant’s substitute address, unless the Secretary of State has determined both of the following:"
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6207(b), the same rule when modifying or maintaining a public record, excluding vital records (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6207.)
  Known gap: Section 6207(a) and section 6207(b) are subdivisions of the same statutory section, so this is a single-section citation for that pairing. This clause quotes the general public-record acceptance rule and its vital-records carve-out; it does not restate the separate Vehicle Code provisions on DMV record suppression referenced in section 6207(e), or the parallel but independently worded agency-acceptance rule for the Chapter 3.2 program in section 6215.5. "Public record" and "bona fide statutory or administrative requirement" are not further defined within this section, and this clause does not resolve how a specific agency would apply that standard to a specific applicant's situation. This is California's own statute and describes only California agencies' obligations.

CONFIDENTIALITY OF A PARTICIPANT'S ACTUAL ADDRESS AND EFFECT ON DISCOVERY
Government Code section 6208 provides that the Secretary of State may not make a program participant's actual address, or a participant's name change, available for inspection or copying, except if requested by a law enforcement agency, directed by a court order to a person named in the order, or after certification has been terminated for use of false information to qualify for the program. Separately, section 6209.7(b)(1) provides that a participant's registration in the program creates a rebuttable presumption that disclosing information about the participant's location and activities -- including current and past residential, work, or school addresses -- would lead to discovery of the participant's actual address, would endanger the participant's safety, and is not authorized; this presumption governs discovery requests generally, including under the Civil Discovery Act.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The Secretary of State may not make a program participant’s address, other than the address designated by the Secretary of State, or a program participant’s name change available for inspection or copying, except under any of the following circumstances:"
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6208, limits on disclosing a participant's actual address (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6208.)
  "The fact that a participant is registered with the program shall create a rebuttable presumption that disclosure of information about the participant’s location and activities during the period of the registration, including, but not limited to, the participant’s current and past residential, work, or school addresses and other location information, would lead to the discovery of the participant’s actual residential address or physical location, would endanger the safety of the participant, and is not authorized."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6209.7(b)(1), rebuttable presumption against disclosure of a participant's location information (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6209.7.)
  Known gap: Section 6208 and section 6209.7(b)(1) are two different statutory sections, so no single-section disclosure applies to that pairing. Section 6209.7 also states that the presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence and is not overcome merely by another party's desire to know the address, and that a court finding the presumption rebutted must state its reasons on the record; this clause does not restate that full rebuttal standard or the separate custody/visitation provisions in section 6209.7(a) and (c). No CourtListener case law search was performed for this clause: this session's one permitted lightweight quota check returned a 429 rate-limit response (125/day exhausted, reset roughly 5.4 hours out), so per this project's practice the clause proceeds on the statutory text alone rather than waiting, and no judicial interpretation of section 6208 or section 6209.7 is represented here. This is California's own statute and does not describe any other state's confidentiality rule.

FEES AND CERTIFICATION LENGTH DIFFER BETWEEN THE TWO CHAPTERS
The two Safe at Home chapters do not use identical fee or duration rules. Chapter 3.1's application section (6206) does not state any application or annual fee for its domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder/dependent adult abuse applicants. By contrast, Government Code section 6215.2(d), in Chapter 3.2, requires submitted applications to be accompanied by a fee set by the Secretary of State not exceeding the actual enrollment cost, permits annual fees to defray the program's maintenance costs, and expressly exempts any applicant who is a patient of a designated health care services facility from both the application fee and the annual fee. On certification length, section 6215.2(f) certifies most Chapter 3.2 applicants for four years, the same period as Chapter 3.1, but certifies a designated health care services facility volunteer only until six months after the volunteer's last date of volunteering with the facility.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Submitted applications shall be accompanied by payment of a fee to be determined by the Secretary of State. This fee shall not exceed the actual costs of enrolling in the program. In addition, annual fees may also be assessed by the Secretary of State to defray the actual costs of maintaining this program. Annual fees assessed by the Secretary of State shall also be used to reimburse the General Fund for any amounts expended from that fund for the purposes of this chapter. No applicant who is a patient of a designated health care services facility shall be required to pay an application fee or the annual fee under this program."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6215.2(d), application and annual fees, with a patient exemption (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6215.2.)
  "Applicants, with the exception of designated health care services facilities volunteers, shall be certified for four years following the date of filing unless the certification is withdrawn, or invalidated before that date. Designated health care services facility volunteers shall be certified until six months from the last date of volunteering with the facility."
  — Cal. Gov't Code § 6215.2(f), four-year certification, with a shorter period for facility volunteers (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=6215.2.)
  Known gap: Section 6215.2(d) and section 6215.2(f) are subdivisions of the same statutory section, so this is a single-section citation for that pairing; the statement that Chapter 3.1 charges no fee is an inference from the absence of fee language in section 6206 rather than an affirmative statutory statement that Chapter 3.1 is free, and this clause does not cite a separate provision expressly saying so. This clause does not state the actual dollar amount of any Chapter 3.2 fee, which section 6215.2(d) leaves to the Secretary of State to set administratively rather than fixing in the statute itself; a current fee amount would need to be confirmed with the Secretary of State's office or its published forms, not this statutory text. This is California's own statute and does not describe any other state's fee structure.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND SIGNATURE
This information sheet was reviewed by Acme, Inc. in connection with a possible application to California's Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program. It summarizes the Government Code provisions described above; it does not itself constitute an application, does not enroll anyone in the program, and does not name or bind any other party, since Safe at Home involves no respondent. Any application must be filed with, and can only be approved by, the Secretary of State's office through the process described in this document.

Signed: ________________________
Acme, Inc.

Date: September 1, 2026
Signed at: Oakland, California

expectedJSON.body: The two Safe at Home chapters do not use identical fee or duration rules. Chapter 3.1's application section (6206) does not state any application or annual fee for its domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, or elder/dependent adult abuse applicants. By contrast, Government Code section 6215.2(d), in Chapter 3.2, requires submitted applications to be accompanied by a fee set by the Secretary of State not exceeding the actual enrollment cost, permits annual fees to defray the program's maintenance costs, and expressly exempts any applicant who is a patient of a designated health care services facility from both the application fee and the annual fee. On certification length, section 6215.2(f) certifies most Chapter 3.2 applicants for four years, the same period as Chapter 3.1, but certifies a designated health care services facility volunteer only until six months after the volunteer's last date of volunteering with the facility.

citations.cite: application and annual fees, with a patient exemption
citations.quote: Submitted applications shall be accompanied by payment of a fee to be determined by the Secretary of State. This fee shall not exceed the actual costs of enrolling in the program. In addition, annual fees may also be assessed by the Secretary of State to defray the actual costs of maintaining this program. Annual fees assessed by the Secretary of State shall also be used to reimburse the General Fund for any amounts expended from that fund for the purposes of this chapter. No applicant who is a patient of a designated health care services facility shall be required to pay an application fee or the annual fee under this program.

citations.cite: four-year certification, with a shorter period for facility volunteers
citations.quote: Applicants, with the exception of designated health care services facilities volunteers, shall be certified for four years following the date of filing unless the certification is withdrawn, or invalidated before that date. Designated health care services facility volunteers shall be certified until six months from the last date of volunteering with the facility.

expectedJSON.gap: Section 6215.2(d) and section 6215.2(f) are subdivisions of the same statutory section, so this is a single-section citation for that pairing; the statement that Chapter 3.1 charges no fee is an inference from the absence of fee language in section 6206 rather than an affirmative statutory statement that Chapter 3.1 is free, and this clause does not cite a separate provision expressly saying so. This clause does not state the actual dollar amount of any Chapter 3.2 fee, which section 6215.2(d) leaves to the Secretary of State to set administratively rather than fixing in the statute itself; a current fee amount would need to be confirmed with the Secretary of State's office or its published forms, not this statutory text. This is California's own statute and does not describe any other state's fee structure.
